key_provisions_or_claims: Study of 245 AI ethics documents using NLP and LLMs finds steep growth since 2017, with about 40% issued by the private sector.
Five principles recur most: beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, autonomy and explicability.
The world of work does not form a distinct thematic cluster in AI ethics guidelines.
Explicit references to the ILO and the fundamental principles and rights at work are rare.
Recommends integrating international labour standards into AI ethics and governance.
annotation.summary_en: ILO blog summarising a study of 245 global AI ethics guidelines, finding convergence on core principles but little connection to labour standards or fundamental rights at work. It argues for integrating ILO norms into AI ethics and governance, addressing algorithmic management, surveillance and displacement.
annotation.title_clean: Governing AI in the World of Work: A review of global ethics guidelines
